correctness.rationale: Each of m base cliques contains a vertex of a dominating set because its diagonal vertex has no outside-clique neighbours. Hence every chosen vertex there sees all omitted vertices in its clique, imposing at most k omissions. A symmetric constant-row-k binary matrix exists by cyclic offsets and yields a dominating set with exactly m-k vertices per clique. On equality, all selected vertices are saturated by k intra-clique omissions, so no cross-row edge can connect selected to omitted; thus the omission matrix must be symmetric. Converse holds. Exact coefficient extraction and the involution/cycle-path enumerations follow by independent combinatorial bijections. The included independent direct graph checker agrees with the matrix method for 2<=m<=5 and checks every subset at m<=3; finite tests are corroborative, not the proof.

value.rationale: The October 2026 Sierpiński k-limited-domination work motivates a natural problem beyond determining only minimum cardinality. An all-optimum classification for every capacity at the first nontrivial recursive level determines exact labelled multiplicities, a symmetry between capacities k and m-k, and a surprising relation with involutions and 2-regular looped components. It gives usable exact counts and a structural explanation even when the number of optimal sets grows; this is not a simple restatement of the known scalar minimum.
